To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the degree of export product diversification is positively related to the size of the economy, to the degree of openness, to the level of income per capita and to the degree of economic integration.
export diversification is higher in countries that are large and not too distant from the economic core, have low trade barriers, and are rich.

(a) export diversification is a function of the size of the domestic market, the size of the foreign market, and the degree of openness of the country; (b) the size of the country is the most important factor; (c) the size of foreign market is the second most important factor; and (d) the degree of openness is the third most important factor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determinants of export diversification and the role played by the degree of diversification in the development process.
the determinants of export diversification, which are not only income related but also related to the size of the domestic market and the size and proximity of foreign markets.
identifying the factors that influence the export diversification of countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, although the size of the market is the most important variable in explaining export diversification, the degree of diversification of exports is also determined by other variables, such as the degree of openness, the level of development and geographical factors.
the export diversification is a function of the size of a country, its geographical location and its trade policy.
export diversification is a complex process that depends on a large number of factors, including those related to market size, distance, income, and trade barriers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general, countries that have a higher degree of export diversifi­cation have a greater potential to grow.
the degree of export specialization is a decreasing function of the degree of market openness and a positive function of the size of domestic and foreign markets.

, for the countries we consider, the degree of export specialization is a function of the country’s size and the size of the markets it is integrated with, as well as the distance from economic core areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, even though income per capita is an important determinant, other features, such as the size of the country, the distance to the core of the economic system and trade barriers are also significant.

the role played by market size is crucial in determining the degree of export specialization or diversification of a country, and that this role becomes more prominent as countries move up the development ladder.
, in the long run, the size and geographical location of countries are the main drivers of the export diversifying process.
